entries.title: Documentation platform
entries.summary: Replaced the hand-authored single-page site with a generated documentation platform covering the whole Atomicals protocol family, the Universe API contracts, executed conformance material, interactive safety tools, and machine readable outputs.

changes.text: Complete protocol reference for Atomicals core concepts, ARC-20, Atomicals NFTs, Containers and DMINT, Realms, Subrealms, Paynames, and the AVM, each labelled by what it applies to and pinned to a source revision.

Thirty one task-oriented guides covering setup, inspection, issuance, minting, transfers, recovery, and trading, each with prerequisites, safety checks, failure cases, and post-broadcast verification.
Validated OpenAPI 3.1 documents for the ARC-20 index, the NFT and Realm index, and Marketplace v1, bound to sanitized route inventories by a check that fails in both directions.
A shared JSON Schema component library where every satoshi and protocol quantity is a decimal string, and every example is validated in CI.
Executed ARC-20 allocation conformance vectors and the engine behind them, implemented from the pinned reference revision and shared by the prose, the visualizer, and the tests.
A generated CLI inventory parsed from the pinned Atomicals JavaScript CLI source, covering every command, argument, and option.
A generated AVM opcode inventory parsed from the beta interpreter source, with the upstream test annotation preserved per opcode.
An AIP registry generated from the upstream proposals plus a separate implementation evidence file, so no proposal is ever marked implemented because it exists.
Interactive local tools: an allocation visualizer, a transaction safety inspector, a Bitwork estimator, a CLI command builder, and an API explorer. None signs, broadcasts, or sends anything anywhere.
An evidence-based ecosystem registry that records unknown rather than guessing, and never treats a network failure as closure.
Machine readable outputs: llms.txt, llms-full.txt, llms.html, a page manifest with content hashes, raw Markdown for every page, a sitemap, and a changelog feed.
A generated TypeScript client for the public read surfaces, with typed errors, pagination helpers, and no embedded credential or default origin.
A local, read-only documentation MCP server that answers from built artefacts, offline, with no mutation, signing, or credential capability.
Eight configured locales with a required page set, a shared glossary, a prohibited mistranslation list, and automatic staleness detection from the English source hash.
The specification, source ledger, and LLM layer, now generated from the content rather than hand maintained, so the compatibility routes cannot drift from the current documentation.
The published site URL now agrees across repository metadata, README links, canonical tags, Open Graph metadata, the sitemap, and the Pages configuration.
